Nora K: quick spike two patterns for long forms: dense inline errors vs spaced summary-first. dropping sketches, thoughts? Ben L: dense inline is faster to fix but visually heavy. favor summary-first on long multi-section forms. keeps scanability. :eyes: Ibrahim A: required markers: faint asterisk + sr-only 'required' after label. avoid blur-validation for optional fields. Toni M: accessibility note: when a summary appears move focus to it (tabindex=-1) and use aria-live="assertive". errors should have aria-describedby and inputs must use aria-invalid. Nora K: destructive control in form (remove billing method): small = inline toggle + undo snackbar; large/irreversible = modal with typed confirm + explicit consequences. support reported accidental removes. Ben L: mobile constraint: summary should collapse to a slim banner "2 problems expand" so it doesn't push content down. ensure it doesn't overlap form controls. Ibrahim A: UX detail: keep helper text baseline aligned with error text. reserve space or use smooth height animation to avoid jumps. Toni M: sample snippet: ```
Enter a project name.
``` Toni M: also recommend announcing "N errors" then linking to fields with anchors, moving focus when a link is activated. Nora K: i'll prototype three variants: (A) dense-inline, (B) summary-banner (collapsed/expanded), (C) optimistic save + undo. will include copy variants and accessibility checklist. Ben L: please include microcopy for destructive modals: title, body, confirm label (e.g., "Delete permanently") and typed-name pattern only for irreversible cases. UX-Bot: created design doc https://redwood/designs/errordensity-checklist includes accessibility checklist and metrics to track (time-to-fix, dismiss-rate, accidental-deletes). Nora K: thanks all react which prototype you prefer and i'll schedule a quick sync with UX Writing.
